quests.title: The Lower Works
quests.description: Azurelode was the richest silver seam in the valley until the pumps stopped and the lower galleries went under in a night. The kobolds were in it inside the week. Grint Halloway has never been able to explain how a creature that cannot read a pump roster knew the pumps had failed.
quests.accept_text:
In through the adit in the western rock, and mind the standing water - it's deeper than the light makes it look and it does not drain anywhere.

Ten should clear the upper galleries. They'll be back. They're always back. I'd settle for walking my own mine without a torch in one hand and an axe in the other.
quests.turn_in_text: Ten, and I got as far as the second landing without stopping. That's further than I've managed since midsummer.

quests.title: What the Water Took
quests.description: Pell Iversen surveyed Azurelode the year before it flooded. His chart is now the only record of what lies under the sump, which makes it worth rather more than the mine and a good deal more than Pell.
quests.accept_text:
The Silver Face, at the top of the workings - you'll know it, the rock goes blue-violet the moment a lamp touches it.

What I need is whether the causeway still stands. My chart says there's a spine of dry rock running to the Face. If the chart's right, the seam is reachable and this is a mine again. If it's wrong, it's a lake with a door.
quests.turn_in_text:
Still standing. Then the chart holds and the Face can be worked.

Don't tell the Overseer yet. He'll put men down there tomorrow and I'd like to know what else is down there first.

quests.title: Measuring a Drowned Mine
quests.description: There are Syndicate men in the flooded galleries and they are not digging. They are measuring - sounding the depth, chalking the walls, running chain along the sump. There is exactly one reason to measure a drowned mine that carefully, and it is to work out what draining it would cost.
quests.accept_text:
Eight, below the causeway. You'll hear the chain before you see the lamps - they sound the depth every ten paces and log it.

Alterac sold the pass to the Horde in the Second War and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords scattered into these hills with nothing. This is what nothing looks like when it finds a silver seam it used to own.
quests.turn_in_text: They were chalking depths on the wall in a hand I recognise from estate maps. That's not a bandit camp's work. Somebody up there still thinks of this valley as property.

quests.title: Smelt It Yourself
quests.description: There is no sense hauling ore to Tarren Mill when the mine's own furnace sits a full six feet above the waterline and has done all along. Halloway wants bars, not baskets, and he would like to know the person bringing them can tell silver from tin.
quests.accept_text:
Cut it off the Face and smelt it - my furnace, or any forge in the valley, I don't care whose.

Five bars. Silver, mind. I've had three men bring me tin this season with a straight face, and tin out of a mine called Azurelode is a special sort of insult.
quests.turn_in_text:
Five, and all five silver.

You'd be amazed how rarely that sentence gets said down here.

quests.title: Grimewick the Drowned
quests.description: The pump house has a kobold foreman in it. He had a hammer he used to beat the pumps back into working whenever they seized, and he was still beating them when the water came over the sill. He has not stopped since, and the pumps have not started.
quests.accept_text:
Pump house, west of the sump.

He took a candle down into a gallery full of pump gas, which is how the whole thing started, and the gas is what killed the shift. Thirty years I've blamed the engineers. Turns out it was one kobold and a candle, and he's still holding the candle.
quests.turn_in_text:
He was still hammering. I could hear it from the second landing and I'd convinced myself it was the water in the pipes.

It was never the water.

quests.title: Overseer Ashlan Silvervein
quests.description: Halloway has a predecessor. Ashlan Silvervein ran Azurelode the night the pumps failed, ordered the lower galleries worked through it, and went down with the shift he refused to call back. He is at the Silver Face. He is still overseeing. Even the kobolds will not go near him.
quests.accept_text:
The Face itself. He carries a mattock with silver worked into the head - a waste of good silver, and he knew it, and he had it made anyway.

I've had his job two years. I'd rather not have it this literally, and I'd rather the men stopped asking me whether he'd have called them back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Would he have called them back? I've been asked that question in every tavern between here and the pass.

He was still standing at the Face with the water up to his chest. I think that's the answer.

quests.title: Cut Square
quests.description: Niall Crag has his measuring chain on the road and has finally got close enough to look at the fort itself. His professional opinion, delivered with some bitterness, is that there is no weak point - the dwarves cut every room in that hold square and put a gate at every narrowing.
quests.accept_text:
Eight of their mountaineers, inside the outer gate. I need the muster yard quiet long enough to measure it.

And look at the walls while you're in there. No chamfer anywhere, no rubble fill, every corner a true corner. That's not a cave they tidied up. They cut a hold out of a mountain, square, on purpose, and I'd admire it more if I weren't trying to get into it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Measured. Twenty-two paces by sixty, and the gates line up to the inch.

I've surveyed six keeps. This is the only one where I could find no mistake to work with.

quests.title: Gatewarden Brannic
quests.description: The outer gate has a warden and the warden is the reason the outer gate is a gate rather than a doorway. Brannic has held the threshold long enough that the Stormpike stopped posting a second man on it.
quests.accept_text:
The outer gate. Bearded axe, a shield scarred in a band at exactly shoulder height, and in fifteen years that axe has only ever swung in one doorway.

He will not come out to you. He has never once come out. You'll have to go to him, in the one place he's had fifteen years to practise standing.
quests.turn_in_text:
He held the threshold until he didn't.

There's a measurement in that too, if you want it: a hold is only as deep as the man at its door is stubborn.

quests.title: Rifle-Sergeant Dunmar
quests.description: The riflemen on the south road are trained, and the training has a name. Dunmar runs the barracks off the muster yard, and Magistrate Pell has worked out that killing riflemen on a road is a tax while killing the man who makes them is a solution.
quests.accept_text:
The barracks, east off the muster yard - there's a sally port up the east wall that reaches it without going through the inner gate.

He sights for the length of that yard and no further, same as his men, because he taught them. Inside that distance he's a man with an empty rifle and a sergeant's temper.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the road patrol is a dozen frightened dwarves with guns and nobody to tell them when to fire.

I'll take frightened. Frightened goes home eventually.

quests.title: The Vault Door
quests.description: There is a door at the back of the Great Hall that the Stormpike keep shut, and a shrine-keeper standing in front of it who has made it his life's work. Nobody in the garrison will say what is behind it. Pell has decided that is itself the answer.
quests.accept_text:
Past the Great Hall, at the vault door.

A smith's hammer, blessed until it stopped being one, and a man who has stood in a doorway so long the dwarves have stopped mentioning him in dispatches. When a garrison stops writing a man down, it's because writing him down means explaining him.
quests.turn_in_text:
Open, then.

And now we have to decide whether we want to know, which is a different question from whether we wanted it open.

quests.title: Thane Korrin Stonewatch
quests.description: Behind the vault door is a crypt, and in the crypt is a thane. He was buried in Dun Garok in an iron circlet by dwarves who swore to hold the ridge, and he did not stay buried, and the garrison above has spent a great many years not discussing the noise.
quests.accept_text:
The Crypt of Dun Garok, past the vault.

Stonewatch Greataxe, and a circlet of iron he was buried in. The oath was to hold the ridge - he is technically still holding it, and that is the single most dwarven sentence I have ever had cause to write in a dispatch.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Stormpike will not thank us and will not admit it happened.

They'll bury him again, deeper, and the next garrison will be told the noise is the wind. That's how a hold keeps a secret: badly, and for centuries.

quests.title: The Undercroft Is Not Empty
quests.description: The Syndicate hold Durnholde's walls and courtyard. They do not go into the undercroft, and Emeline Vask finds that more interesting than anything else about the keep: a garrison with a cellar it will not use has a reason, and reasons are what she is for.
quests.accept_text:
Eight of whatever is down there. The stair is behind the Lord's Hall.

These were the keep's own garrison - Lordaeron's men, the ones who were here when it fell. They didn't leave. The Syndicate have simply built their camp on top of them and agreed not to go downstairs, which is the most honest thing I know about the Syndicate.
quests.turn_in_text:
Lordaeron livery under the rot on all eight. I thought so.

They held this keep, they lost it, and they have been underneath everyone who's held it since.

The gatehouse, first thing through the archway.

He'll sound the alarm before he fights - that's his whole function and he's good at it. If you want to get further into that keep than the bailey, the bell has to stop before the shouting starts.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet, then. For the first time in two years, quiet at the gate.

Go further in while it lasts.

quests.title: Houndmaster Sable
quests.description: The kennels on the keep's east side are the reason nobody has ever got across the bailey unseen. Sable's hounds learned the work faster than her recruits did, which she says to recruits, in front of the hounds.
quests.accept_text:
The kennels, east bailey, through the breach.

She sets the pack on first and fights second. Kill the handler and the pack is a dozen dogs with nobody shouting at them - they'll scatter inside a minute. Try it the other way round and you'll be fighting dogs until there are no more dogs.
quests.turn_in_text:
The pack went over the wall and didn't come back. Dogs are sensible.

That's the bailey crossable now, which is two years of my reports made obsolete in an afternoon. I'm delighted.

quests.title: Magister Yvaine
quests.description: The Syndicate's binders are trained, and training needs a trainer. Yvaine holds the west tower with a staff of Alterac work that somebody re-cut with less patience than the original maker had, and she is the reason a scrap camp in the hills can field wizards at all.
quests.accept_text:
West tower, off the ring. One door, no other way out, which cuts both ways.

She's Alterac court - properly trained, properly taught, and reduced to teaching hedge-binders in a ruin. There'll be a ledger of names on her. Bring it. I want to know who she's been training and where they went.
quests.turn_in_text:
Names and postings, in a court hand.

She was training them and sending them out, and about half these postings aren't in Hillsbrad at all. This goes north tonight.

quests.title: The Turnkey
quests.description: There was a gaoler in Durnholde, and a gaoler in Durnholde in those years means one thing. Emeline Vask would like him dealt with, and she has not entirely separated the scholarship from the rest of it, and she knows that about herself.
quests.accept_text:
The undercroft, past the revenants. Thirty keys on a chain and he swings the lot as one.

He kept the cells. In this keep, in those years, there was one prisoner worth keeping and a boy doesn't hold his own keys. I'm aware that's not a military reason. I'm asking anyway.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thirty keys, and not one lock left in that cellar worth turning.

It isn't scholarship and I'll not pretend it was. Thank you for not making me explain it.

quests.title: Baron Aliden Perenolde
quests.description: Gavin's ledger named who paid. Yvaine's postings named who was sent. Godfrey's remnant, two zones back in Silverpine, named what a dispossessed noble will do to get a country back. All three threads run to one man sitting in the Lord's Hall of a keep his family never owned, holding a court for a kingdom that was dissolved fifteen years ago.
quests.accept_text:
The Lord's Hall, at the heart of the ring. You've done the work that makes this possible and I'd rather you knew it: without the fence's ledger and the magister's postings I'd have sent you in to kill a squatter.

Alterac sold the Alliance to the Horde and his father signed it. The Alliance dissolved the kingdom and left the family their titles, because titles cost nothing. This is what fifteen years of carrying a title and no country does to a man.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's finished.

The Syndicate won't end - there's always another cousin with a sash. But the man who could pay wizards and buy a valley's thieves is on the floor of a hall his family had no claim to, and the ledger, the postings and the name all go north together.

You walked three roads for this. I'll see every one of them is in the dispatch.
